title: In-process relay reads a 400 as Invalid; the HTTP client reads it as Refused
summary: The in-process relay maps a malformed request to Invalid; a wallet's HTTP client reads the same 400 as Refused(Other). The doc comment says the two match.
description: services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:382-389 `relayed()` claims to give "the answer the HTTP client would read" but maps store Error::Invalid to table_relay::Error::Invalid. Over HTTP that error is served as 400 (lib.rs:363) and crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs:50 `answer_error` reads every non-429 4xx as Refused. Fix: derive the mapping from the reader itself, `table_relay::answer_error(StatusCode::from(e).as_u16(), b"")`, so one table decides both paths. No caller branches on the difference today (crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:235-262 collapses all errors; services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs:984 maps non-Full to Unavailable), so this is a correctness-of-contract fix with a false comment.
flow:
- RelayApi::send(&store, known, "not-a-jws") -> Mailbox::send -> Error::Invalid -> relayed() -> Invalid
- the same body over HTTP -> 400 -> answer_error -> Refused(Other)
- fix: relayed(e) = answer_error(StatusCode::from(e).as_u16(), b"")
impact_text: The in-process and HTTP relays agree on every store refusal, and the doc comment becomes true. Nothing should break: no caller tells Invalid from Refused on this path.
evaluation:
Claim: quality - in-process and HTTP error classes agree for every store error
Before: 2 of 3 store errors agree (Full, Missing); Invalid differs (read at lib.rs:384-389 vs table-relay lib.rs:47-58)
After: 3 of 3, pinned by test every_store_refusal_reads_in_process_as_the_http_client_reads_its_status (in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)
Method: simulation - the test is written but could not be run: this machine refuses to execute freshly built binaries (os error 5), so red/green was not observed
Result: better
Gate: none
body:
## Summary
The in-process relay maps a malformed request to Invalid; a wallet's HTTP client reads the same 400 as Refused(Other). The doc comment says the two match.

## Description
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:382-389 `relayed()` claims to give "the answer the HTTP client would read" but maps store Error::Invalid to table_relay::Error::Invalid. Over HTTP that error is served as 400 (lib.rs:363) and crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs:50 `answer_error` reads every non-429 4xx as Refused. Fix: derive the mapping from the reader itself, `table_relay::answer_error(StatusCode::from(e).as_u16(), b"")`, so one table decides both paths. No caller branches on the difference today (crates/table-runtime/src/relay.rs:235-262 collapses all errors; services/house-seller/src/hosted.rs:984 maps non-Full to Unavailable), so this is a correctness-of-contract fix with a false comment.

## Flow
- RelayApi::send(&store, known, "not-a-jws") -> Mailbox::send -> Error::Invalid -> relayed() -> Invalid
- the same body over HTTP -> 400 -> answer_error -> Refused(Other)
- fix: relayed(e) = answer_error(StatusCode::from(e).as_u16(), b"")

## Expected impact
The in-process and HTTP relays agree on every store refusal, and the doc comment becomes true. Nothing should break: no caller tells Invalid from Refused on this path.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - in-process and HTTP error classes agree for every store error
Before: 2 of 3 store errors agree (Full, Missing); Invalid differs (read at lib.rs:384-389 vs table-relay lib.rs:47-58)
After: 3 of 3, pinned by test every_store_refusal_reads_in_process_as_the_http_client_reads_its_status (in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)
Method: simulation - the test is written but could not be run: this machine refuses to execute freshly built binaries (os error 5), so red/green was not observed
Result: better
Gate: none

title: HTTP relay client sends a generation no relay issues; in-process relay refuses it
summary: Client::poll checks wait and after but not the generation length; the in-process poll and the /sync route both refuse a generation over 32 characters.
description: crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs:250 bounds wait and after only. services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:411-414 (in-process) and :525-528 (/sync) also refuse generation.len() > 32. So the same bad input is Invalid in process and a network round trip ending in Refused(Other) over HTTP. The literal 32 appears in four places (table-relay lib.rs:69, rendezvous lib.rs:413 and :527). Fix: one `GENERATION_LEN` constant in table-relay, used at all four, plus the check in Client::poll.
flow:
- Client::poll(mailbox, "a"*33, 0, 0) -> request goes out -> server 400 -> Refused(Other)
- fix: refuse before sending -> Invalid, matching the in-process path
impact_text: Both RelayApi implementations refuse the same inputs the same way, and the generation bound has one definition. Callers only ever pass "" or a validated 32-hex generation, so nothing in the tree changes behaviour.
evaluation:
Claim: quality - both RelayApi implementations refuse the same poll inputs
Before: 2 of 3 poll bounds checked client-side (wait, after); generation unchecked (lib.rs:250)
After: 3 of 3, pinned by test a_poll_with_a_generation_no_relay_issues_is_refused_before_any_request (in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)
Method: simulation - test written, not runnable on this machine (os error 5 on built binaries)
Result: better
Gate: none
body:
## Summary
Client::poll checks wait and after but not the generation length; the in-process poll and the /sync route both refuse a generation over 32 characters.

## Description
crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs:250 bounds wait and after only. services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:411-414 (in-process) and :525-528 (/sync) also refuse generation.len() > 32. So the same bad input is Invalid in process and a network round trip ending in Refused(Other) over HTTP. The literal 32 appears in four places (table-relay lib.rs:69, rendezvous lib.rs:413 and :527). Fix: one `GENERATION_LEN` constant in table-relay, used at all four, plus the check in Client::poll.

## Flow
- Client::poll(mailbox, "a"*33, 0, 0) -> request goes out -> server 400 -> Refused(Other)
- fix: refuse before sending -> Invalid, matching the in-process path

## Expected impact
Both RelayApi implementations refuse the same inputs the same way, and the generation bound has one definition. Callers only ever pass "" or a validated 32-hex generation, so nothing in the tree changes behaviour.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - both RelayApi implementations refuse the same poll inputs
Before: 2 of 3 poll bounds checked client-side (wait, after); generation unchecked (lib.rs:250)
After: 3 of 3, pinned by test a_poll_with_a_generation_no_relay_issues_is_refused_before_any_request (in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)
Method: simulation - test written, not runnable on this machine (os error 5 on built binaries)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: No test pins the 400 bounds of the /sync and /envelopes poll routes
summary: The poll routes refuse wait > 25, after > 256, generation > 32 and unknown query fields, but no test sends any of them over the router.
description: services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:462 and :525-528 hold the route bounds. Grepping services/rendezvous/tests and crates/table-runtime/src/relay_tests.rs for sync/envelopes queries finds only in-bound requests (tests/serve.rs:233, :243; relay_tests.rs:319). Deleting any bound today leaves the suite green. The prepared test sends six out-of-bound queries (expects 400) and two at the bound (expects 200). Seeded control: delete the `q.after > MAX_MESSAGES` check and the after=257 case must go red, because an unknown generation resets the cursor to 0.
flow:
- GET /v1/mailbox/{h}/sync?wait=26 -> 400 (unpinned)
- the same for after=257, a 33-char generation, an unknown field, envelopes?wait=26, envelopes?after past the end
- build: add the test, then seed one deleted bound and watch it go red
impact_text: A refactor that drops a route bound fails CI instead of shipping. Test-only change.
evaluation:
Claim: quality - route bounds pinned by a test
Before: 0 of 6 out-of-bound queries asserted (grep of the tests)
After: 6 of 6, with a seeded control (test the_poll_routes_refuse_every_out_of_bound_query_and_accept_the_bound in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)
Method: simulation - test written, not runnable on this machine (os error 5)
Result: better
Gate: none

## Summary
The poll routes refuse wait > 25, after > 256, generation > 32 and unknown query fields, but no test sends any of them over the router.

## Description
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:462 and :525-528 hold the route bounds. Grepping services/rendezvous/tests and crates/table-runtime/src/relay_tests.rs for sync/envelopes queries finds only in-bound requests (tests/serve.rs:233, :243; relay_tests.rs:319). Deleting any bound today leaves the suite green. The prepared test sends six out-of-bound queries (expects 400) and two at the bound (expects 200). Seeded control: delete the `q.after > MAX_MESSAGES` check and the after=257 case must go red, because an unknown generation resets the cursor to 0.

- GET /v1/mailbox/{h}/sync?wait=26 -> 400 (unpinned)
- the same for after=257, a 33-char generation, an unknown field, envelopes?wait=26, envelopes?after past the end
- build: add the test, then seed one deleted bound and watch it go red

## Expected impact
A refactor that drops a route bound fails CI instead of shipping. Test-only change.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - route bounds pinned by a test
Before: 0 of 6 out-of-bound queries asserted (grep of the tests)
After: 6 of 6, with a seeded control (test the_poll_routes_refuse_every_out_of_bound_query_and_accept_the_bound in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)

title: Expiry sweep drops a mailbox without waking its long-polls; remove does
summary: Inner::sweep removes expired mailboxes silently, while remove() notifies their waiters, so a poll on an expired mailbox sleeps out its full wait.
description: services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:82-92 `sweep` retains live boxes without calling `changed.notify_waiters()`. services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:353-355 `remove` notifies. A /sync long-poll holding the expired box's Notify only wakes at its timeout (up to 25 s), then reads 404. Fix: notify inside sweep's !live branch.
flow:
- wallet long-polls /sync wait=25 on mailbox M
- M passes its 24 h expiry; another create/send sweeps it
- poll keeps sleeping until 25 s, then 404
- fix: sweep notifies -> poll re-reads at once -> 404
impact_text: A wallet learns its mailbox expired up to 25 s sooner, once per mailbox per day. Small; a wake-up only causes an extra read under the lock.
evaluation:
Claim: resilience - a poll ends when its mailbox is dropped
Before: poll returns at its 25 s timeout (read from lib.rs:82-92, :544)
After: returns at the sweep, pinned by test a_long_poll_on_a_mailbox_that_expires_ends_when_the_relay_drops_it (in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)
Method: simulation - test written, not runnable on this machine (os error 5)
Result: better
Gate: none
body:
## Summary
Inner::sweep removes expired mailboxes silently, while remove() notifies their waiters, so a poll on an expired mailbox sleeps out its full wait.

## Description
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:82-92 `sweep` retains live boxes without calling `changed.notify_waiters()`. services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:353-355 `remove` notifies. A /sync long-poll holding the expired box's Notify only wakes at its timeout (up to 25 s), then reads 404. Fix: notify inside sweep's !live branch.

## Flow
- wallet long-polls /sync wait=25 on mailbox M
- M passes its 24 h expiry; another create/send sweeps it
- poll keeps sleeping until 25 s, then 404
- fix: sweep notifies -> poll re-reads at once -> 404

## Expected impact
A wallet learns its mailbox expired up to 25 s sooner, once per mailbox per day. Small; a wake-up only causes an extra read under the lock.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a poll ends when its mailbox is dropped
Before: poll returns at its 25 s timeout (read from lib.rs:82-92, :544)
After: returns at the sweep, pinned by test a_long_poll_on_a_mailbox_that_expires_ends_when_the_relay_drops_it (in .claude/scan-sweep/findings/relay-sweep-2026-10-23.patch)
Method: simulation - test written, not runnable on this machine (os error 5)
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Standalone relay ignores SIGTERM, so docker/systemd stops skip its graceful shutdown
summary: services/rendezvous/src/main.rs waits only for ctrl-c; its sibling services/house-seller/src/main.rs also waits for SIGTERM.
description: services/rendezvous/src/main.rs:17-23 resolves the shutdown future on ctrl_c (SIGINT) only, though the comment promises in-flight requests finish. A container or service manager stops with SIGTERM, whose default action kills the process at once: 25 s long-polls are reset and serve_with's GracefulShutdown (serve.rs:234) never runs. services/house-seller/src/main.rs:13-34 already has the ctrl-c-or-SIGTERM `shutdown()`. The standalone binary is not in render.yaml, but README.md:129 tells users to run their own `services/rendezvous`. Fix: the same select! over ctrl_c and unix SIGTERM, or one shared `rendezvous::stop_signal()` that both mains use (the second touches house-seller and is out of this context's paths).
flow:
- docker stop <relay> -> SIGTERM -> process killed
- open long-polls are reset; clients see Unavailable and back off
- fix: SIGTERM resolves `stop` -> no new accepts, polls finish, exit 0
impact_text: Self-hosted relays stop cleanly on deploys. Today a wallet sees one Unavailable per open poll per stop. Nothing should break; the unix branch is cfg-gated.
evaluation:
Claim: resilience - the binary exits gracefully on its host's stop signal
Before: signals handled {SIGINT} (main.rs:20) vs sibling {SIGINT, SIGTERM} (house-seller main.rs:15,21)
After: {SIGINT, SIGTERM}
Method: simulation - the instrument is a #[cfg(unix)] test that spawns CARGO_BIN_EXE_rendezvous with PORT=0, sends SIGTERM, and asserts exit status 0 (before: killed by signal 15). It needs a Linux runner (CI ubuntu, or a worker in WSL/Docker); this Windows machine cannot send SIGTERM and could not run built binaries this session
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: #[cfg(unix)] integration test: spawn CARGO_BIN_EXE_rendezvous (PORT=0), kill -TERM, assert exit 0 within 5 s
body:
## Summary
services/rendezvous/src/main.rs waits only for ctrl-c; its sibling services/house-seller/src/main.rs also waits for SIGTERM.

## Description
services/rendezvous/src/main.rs:17-23 resolves the shutdown future on ctrl_c (SIGINT) only, though the comment promises in-flight requests finish. A container or service manager stops with SIGTERM, whose default action kills the process at once: 25 s long-polls are reset and serve_with's GracefulShutdown (serve.rs:234) never runs. services/house-seller/src/main.rs:13-34 already has the ctrl-c-or-SIGTERM `shutdown()`. The standalone binary is not in render.yaml, but README.md:129 tells users to run their own `services/rendezvous`. Fix: the same select! over ctrl_c and unix SIGTERM, or one shared `rendezvous::stop_signal()` that both mains use (the second touches house-seller and is out of this context's paths).

## Flow
- docker stop <relay> -> SIGTERM -> process killed
- open long-polls are reset; clients see Unavailable and back off
- fix: SIGTERM resolves `stop` -> no new accepts, polls finish, exit 0

## Expected impact
Self-hosted relays stop cleanly on deploys. Today a wallet sees one Unavailable per open poll per stop. Nothing should break; the unix branch is cfg-gated.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the binary exits gracefully on its host's stop signal
Before: signals handled {SIGINT} (main.rs:20) vs sibling {SIGINT, SIGTERM} (house-seller main.rs:15,21)
After: {SIGINT, SIGTERM}
Method: simulation - the instrument is a #[cfg(unix)] test that spawns CARGO_BIN_EXE_rendezvous with PORT=0, sends SIGTERM, and asserts exit status 0 (before: killed by signal 15). It needs a Linux runner (CI ubuntu, or a worker in WSL/Docker); this Windows machine cannot send SIGTERM and could not run built binaries this session
Result: better
Gate: none

title: GET /envelopes has no in-tree reader and duplicates the /sync long-poll
summary: The legacy read route GET /v1/mailbox/{hash}/envelopes has no client in this tree. Its long-poll is a second copy of /sync's.
description: services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:377 routes GET /envelopes to `read` (:457-477), whose long-poll duplicates `sync` (:520-546). crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs uses /sync for polls and /envelopes only for POST (:237). `git log -S` on the table-relay client finds no GET /envelopes ever. Only tests read it. docs/features/pairing-relay-house.md:96 still lists it as part of the relay contract, and self-hosted or older wallets outside this tree cannot be enumerated. Removing it is a public-contract call.
flow:
- decide: retire GET /envelopes (doc + route + read handler + its tests) or keep it as documented contract
- if retired: one long-poll implementation stays; the permit test (tests/serve.rs:244) drops its envelopes arm
impact_text: About 40 lines less surface and one long-poll path instead of two. An unknown external reader would start getting 405.
evaluation:
Claim: quality - one poll route instead of two
Before: 2 long-poll implementations; 0 non-test readers of GET /envelopes in tree (grep + git log -S)
After: 1
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep over git ls-files; external readers cannot be measured
Result: better
Gate: contract
body:
## Summary
The legacy read route GET /v1/mailbox/{hash}/envelopes has no client in this tree. Its long-poll is a second copy of /sync's.

## Description
services/rendezvous/src/lib.rs:377 routes GET /envelopes to `read` (:457-477), whose long-poll duplicates `sync` (:520-546). crates/table-relay/src/lib.rs uses /sync for polls and /envelopes only for POST (:237). `git log -S` on the table-relay client finds no GET /envelopes ever. Only tests read it. docs/features/pairing-relay-house.md:96 still lists it as part of the relay contract, and self-hosted or older wallets outside this tree cannot be enumerated. Removing it is a public-contract call.

## Flow
- decide: retire GET /envelopes (doc + route + read handler + its tests) or keep it as documented contract
- if retired: one long-poll implementation stays; the permit test (tests/serve.rs:244) drops its envelopes arm

## Expected impact
About 40 lines less surface and one long-poll path instead of two. An unknown external reader would start getting 405.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one poll route instead of two
Before: 2 long-poll implementations; 0 non-test readers of GET /envelopes in tree (grep + git log -S)
After: 1
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep over git ls-files; external readers cannot be measured
Result: better
Gate: contract
